artifacts.summary: Line-level fix points for Defect A (unvalidated post-`--` lake subcommand), Defect B (fingerprint blind to build scope, no audible replay signal), and Defect C (undocumented wait idiom), plus a mapping of acceptance criteria onto the existing 13-case-plus-mutation test harness's reusable scaffolding (FAKE_LAKE_COUNTER, exit-passthrough pattern, grep-based regression cases, scratch-copy sed mutation pattern).

memory_candidates.content: In lake-build-guard.sh's arg parser, lake_args (the post-subcommand vector eventually handed to `lake`) is populated by TWO independent branches of the same while-loop: the explicit `--)` branch (shift; lake_args+=("$@"); break) and the bare catch-all `*)` branch for args with no leading `--`. A validation fix targeting only one branch silently misses invocations shaped like the other. The single point where both paths have already converged is right after the parsing while-loop exits, before dispatch -- that is the correct place for any lake_args[0] validation, not inside either branch.

lake-build-guard.sh's result record is a flat grep-readable key=value file (never sourced, deliberately, so record content is never executed as shell) written by write_inflight_record()/finalize_record() and read via a single get_record_field() helper. Extending this record's schema with a new concern-specific field (e.g. a build-scope key alongside the existing pre_fingerprint/post_fingerprint tree-staleness fields) is a low-risk, same-shape extension -- prefer this over folding a new concern into an existing field's hash, since one named field per concern keeps each comparison independently debuggable.
